circuit.title: Central complex head-direction (ring attractor) core
circuit.rationale: The fly's head-direction system is the best-characterised recurrent circuit in the insect brain and the textbook example of a biological ring attractor: a single 'bump' of activity in the ellipsoid body tracks heading, EPG neurons carry the bump, PEN neurons shift it in proportion to angular velocity, PEG neurons feed it back, and Delta7 neurons provide the global inhibition that keeps exactly one bump alive. That makes it an unusually good target for a propagation demo: the circuit is strongly recurrent (so propagation does something more interesting than a feed-forward cascade), it mixes excitation and inhibition, and its expected qualitative behaviour is documented, so a viewer can sanity-check the simulation against published biology. It is also small enough (~150 neurons, ~2.7k edges) to render and simulate interactively in a browser, unlike the full ~140k-neuron connectome.
